decisions.reason: As a newly launched sensor module with its own page, it still has unresolved market potential and the option value of waiting likely exceeds the modest cost of keeping it available.
Because it is a direct successor to an earlier voltage measurement module, the launch already reveals fit with an established product line and makes near-term withdrawal unlikely.
A software-based MQTT proxy has low carrying costs and complements the firm's modular electronics ecosystem, so management would keep the option open while demand becomes clearer.
The CAN bus interface module is more niche and was only mentioned rather than strongly featured, but as a complementary interface product it is still worth retaining for now.
The carbon dioxide sensor module was given its own page and addresses a recognizable sensing use case, so the firm would likely continue observing adoption before abandoning it.

The touch panel accessory is a newer peripheral with somewhat less certain standalone demand, but its complementarity with the firm's installed base supports keeping it on the market for another year.
